text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime minister secures confidence vote.
- Ariel Sharon meets prime minister, Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel.
- Foreign ministry sources: Politics paralyse Middle East peacemaking.
- Attorney General asks police to investigate signs assailing Communications Minister Limor Livnat.
- Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat improves ties with Iran.
- Israeli ambassador to U.S.: Israel wants U.S. aid to Palestinian Authority conditioned on action against terrorism.
- Former Finance Minister Dan Meridor: Budget-cut plan on prime minister's desk for a month. Benjamin Netanyahu claims proposal still being studied by Treasury.
- Israel, Poland to sign trade pact next month.
- Africa Israel plans $120 million industrial park in Lod.
GLOBES
- Dollar soars 1.37 percent to 3.484 shekels.
- Koor Industries postpones U.S. bond issue to raise $300 million in wake of foreign exchange policy change.
HAARETZ
- Ariel Sharon: Additional authority -- a condition to taking the finance ministry. Expectation government won't fall in no-confidence vote.
- IMF deputy chief tells Haaretz: Sharon must immediately cut the budget to prove he has changed direction.
- For the first time Reform Jews in the United States will encourage immigration to Israel in their platform.
- Israel astonished by "one-sided declaration" of the eight industrialised states in the matter of negotiations with the Palestinians.
- Knesset members seek to double pensions over age 55.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Ariel Sharon demands wider responsibilities.
- Sources close to Secretary of State Madeleine Albright say she will think twice before meeting Israeli Ambassador Eliahu Ben-Elissar again.
- Israeli intelligence sources say: "An outbreak is expected in the territories to break up the Palestinian Authority."
MAARIV

- Foreign Minister David Levy and Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai: "We're headed for disaster." At a meeting they voiced concern over planned makeup of the government and used such words as "We're headed for a catastrophe" and "We're dealing with nonsense instead of preventing the expected explosion in the territories."
